answers.assumption_check: Assumes a --scratch bus's transit table is a throwaway (BusDevice.scratch via __main__.py:60) and dropped at its exit, so what survives an exit is only what serve already writes to the home (final_flush's spill, hand_over_asks' asks file). Idle exit is therefore allowed only when neither has anything to write: no connection open, no ask in flight, no undelivered row. Assumes N=1800 s, which is a HYPOTHESIS because bus.log carries no ask timing (measured); D2 makes it measurable.

All are carried in decisions.

answers.falsifier_check: Three clauses, one tooth each, horizon the red-first proof. (1) Only a --scratch bus idles out: a scratch serve with nothing open past N exits with stop cause 'idle', and a serve with scratch=False under the same N is still serving after it. (2) Nothing is lost: idle never fires while a connection is open, an ask is in flight or a row is undelivered, and after an idle exit a post to a recipient subscribed before the exit is delivered by the respawned bus at the same home. (3) N is read: unset CAIRN_BUS_IDLE_S gives N=1800, and every stop record carries idle_s_max.
answers.gates_bound: code-seam: proof gate = bin/cairn test over the red-first proof, sealed by the tester; hollow gate = cairn test --hollow; verdict gate at PROVED; feeds back to origin (this ticket's measured) on failure.
answers.missing_check: It does not remove the leaked homes (a caller's mktemp is the caller's to clean). It does not decide which verb spawned each of the 31 (bus.log gives time and cwd only).

bullets.text: The home-gone guard was already built and never fired: no leaked home was ever removed. The leak is a caller that never ends, so the bound belongs to the bus's own idleness.
